turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mrs Naidoo, in you come. Is it the knee today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, doctor. The right one. It gets me on the stairs, going down.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Last winter, or the one before. I can't date it.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Three months. She was already complaining when I started the February shifts.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it's more than three months. Six months, well, maybe longer. I don't know, doctor, I'm hopeless with the when.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Downstairs only?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Down is the worst. Up I use the rail. Flat ground is fine if I don't hurry.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Night-time?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Some nights, a deep ache. I roll over and it settles. Not every night.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it swell?
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It does. Evenings, the right knee looks puffy when she puts her feet up.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It does not swell. I don't know what she thinks she's seeing. It hurts, that's all.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning stiffness?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): A few minutes, then it eases. Not the whole morning.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Give way?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Locking?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other joints?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, just this knee.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Shame, the drive was the worst part. That robot by the mall had us sitting there for ages, hey.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, the traffic. Did you see the Proteas? My grandson shouted at the TV the whole afternoon.
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Little Sipho, seven years old, already picking the team. He says they need a spinner. He had his shoes on the wrong feet and just carried on.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): And he reckons the weather man is useless. So hot, then the wind. We sat on the stoep with rusks and he talked nonsense.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He wants a bakkie one day, not a car. We were still laughing in the waiting room. Anyway, that's not why we came.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Gel, or tablets?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Diclofenac gel, the one from Clicks. I rub it on the right knee, morning and bedtime.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): And tablets?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes diclofenac from the chemist, when the pain is bad. One tablet. The box says 50 milligrams.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two tablets. I pop two of those fifties when she's really sore. She's forgetting.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I was sure it was one. If she says two, maybe two. I lose track.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Daily?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only on the sore days. I can't say how many.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything before that?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Naproxen. Stopped it in March. 250 milligrams twice a day, from the GP, for the knee.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you take the tramadol script?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I never took it. I never even collected it.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stomach problems with these pills? Yes or no.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No stomach problems.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nausea?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Black stool?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, heartburn. I do get that. I shouldn't have said no just now. After the diclofenac tablets, some afternoons.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every time you take them?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Not every time. A burn behind the breastbone when I have. That's the truth of it.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): High blood pressure, for years. Enalapril, ten milligrams every morning.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Correct. Ten milligrams with the morning tea. That one she takes properly.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Known hypertension, ongoing. Medicine allergies?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Never have.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): A glass of wine at Christmas. Otherwise no. I don't know if that's worth mentioning.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still working?
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Retired. I taught at the primary school. Ten years out of it now.
[SEG0061] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm her carer on weekdays, mornings and evenings. She lives alone in the flat otherwise. I'm not family.
[SEG0062] person_1 (DOCTOR): On the bed. Right knee first.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): No effusion. I cannot feel any swelling today.
[SEG0064] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medial joint line is tender. There is crepitus on bending, and flexion stops short.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): Eina. Ja, that's the spot.
[SEG0066] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left knee is fine. Hips are fine.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight?
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0069] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Bathroom scale said 94 the other week. The scale is ancient, mind you.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): That scale lies. I don't know the number. The skirts are tighter, so maybe I've picked up. That's all.
[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not recording a weight. Less load on the knee — ease off the biscuits and the rusks.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll try. I don't know if I can. The rusks are a habit.
[SEG0073] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm calling it osteoarthritis of the right knee for now. Not nailed down.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I don't really know what to do with that.
[SEG0075] person_1 (DOCTOR): Physio, or a steroid injection into the knee. I am not deciding, and I am not booking either today.
[SEG0076] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Needles worry me. The stairs worry me more.
[SEG0077] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She'll do physio if I take her. The injection she ducks every time we mention it.

[SEG0078] person_1 (DOCTOR): Next visit we choose, if it still needs it. Keep the gel morning and night. Stop the diclofenac tablets, they match the heartburn. Paracetamol, one gram up to four times a day — I'm writing that script.
[SEG0079] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in six weeks. Reception will slot you in.

spec.situation: Older patient with knee pain going down stairs and at night; uses diclofenac gel and sometimes tablets from the pharmacy; says no stomach problems and then mentions heartburn; weight discussed; physio or injection discussed, not decided.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Pain and stair aggravation supported; duration 'approximately 3 to 6 months' is disputed/uncertain.
bad.text: Right knee pain (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, duration=approximately 3 to 6 months, temporality=current, body_site=right knee, aggravating_factors=going down stairs, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Right knee pain is also aggravated by going upstairs (uses the rail) and flat ground is fine if she does not hurry.
The oral diclofenac tablet strength is 50 mg, and there is an unresolved discrepancy whether she takes one tablet or two tablets when the pain is bad.
The patient did not take or collect the tramadol prescription.
Stomach problems was initially denied, then corrected: she does have heartburn after diclofenac tablets; this specific negation reversal is not recorded as a negative-finding discrepancy.
Physiotherapy versus steroid injection was discussed, but the doctor explicitly said no decision and no booking would be made today; the choice would be made at the next visit if still needed.
